transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jin Park (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CTO, Nexa Labs), Diego Ruiz (Head of ML), Priya Srinivasan (Infra)

Summary (auto): quick wins from last week on cache priming; dug into p95/p99 tail; planning next perf run at higher concurrency.

00:00 Samir: okay everyone, thanks for joining, quick check, can you hear me?
00:07 Maya: yes, loud and clear, thanks Samir
00:12 Jin: awesome, i'll share my screen in a sec, got the benchmark dashboard open
00:20 Diego: real quick - we ran some internal microbenchmarks too, i'll post the raw numbers after this
00:30 Samir: sweet, agenda: run through the benchmark sheet, call out where redwood beat baseline, where baseline still edges us, and agree on next test (2k conc) and security docs to hand off
01:05 Jin: okay loading the p50/p95/p99 chart - first thing to call out, median latency for our tuned model on your test prompt set: redwood p50 ~65ms, baseline p50 ~78ms, p95 redwood ~210ms, baseline p95 ~320ms
01:35 Maya: those p95 numbers look good on your side, can you remind me which machine type and model quantization you used?
01:42 Jin: sure - this run was on our hosted inference with a dedicated pool style profile but still on shared infra for the pilot; model is the open-7b quantized to int8 (we used per-channel quantization). GPU type is A100 equivalent, nvlink enabled; baseline ran on CloudX c5-like instance with different kernel set - they had slightly lower single token latency on cold start
02:10 Diego: strange, baseline had lower cold-start single token? how large was the batch?
02:16 Jin: baseline's single-request p50 on an empty KV cache was low, but once you crank concurrency the cpu hits and context switching add up; our continuous batching and kv prefix cache reduce per-token work across requests, which is why sustained throughput favored us
02:45 Priya: what's the throughput numbers? tokens per second or requests per second? we need both for capacity planning
02:52 Jin: good point - tokens/sec for your prompt mix: Redwood sustained ~12.5k tokens/s per GPU under steady 500 QPS with batching; baseline was ~8.2k tokens/s under same shape. RPS wise at 500 concurrent connections, Redwood sustained 480 RPS with median response size, baseline sustained ~320 RPS
03:20 Diego: and tail latency at higher conc, p99?
03:25 Jin: p99 at 500 QPS: Redwood ~480ms, baseline ~1.1s. When we move to dedicated pool with slightly bigger batch windows we get p99 down to ~320ms in our internal runs
03:50 Maya: those are important numbers. We care p95/p99 more than p50 for UX. Any idea what's driving the baseline's tail? memory thrash or KV cache misses?
04:05 Jin: it's mostly queueing + context switching on their infra, and also they don't do cross-request kv caching so repeated prefix tokens are recomputed. We saw large gains after priming the KV cache for common prefixes - 20-30% p95 improvements on average
04:30 Diego: can you describe the KV priming you did? we need reproducible steps for our infra team
04:36 Jin: yes - we ran a small priming routine that issues the typical prompt prefixes with a short TTL and warms the kv cache; i put the script in the sheet under the "priming" tab, link in chat
04:52 Maya: got it. On quantization: any regression in output quality with int8? we can't afford hallucination jumps
04:58 Jin: we ran the eval prompts from your eval set - quality delta was within noise, rouge/bleu style autometrics and also human spot-checks showed no meaningful regression. I'll attach the eval gist. the one caveat is some edge cases with very long context had slightly more token deletions, but that's tunable with kv chunk sizes
05:30 Priya: network question - for the private deployment later we will need VPC peering and specific egress rules, do you have a sample network diagram?
05:40 Samir: yes, we'll share the network diagram and onboarding checklist. I can get that out tonight.
05:45 Maya: perfect. back to perf: what's the plan for the 2k concurrency run? do we need us to provision traffic generator or do you handle it?
06:00 Jin: we can run from Redwood side but prefer you to run one of your traffic profiles so it's more realistic; we can also replicate locally if you want. For the next run we'll test: 2k conc steady for 15 minutes, cache primed and unprimed, and measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput. We'll also capture raw histograms and CPU/GPU utilization
06:30 Diego: please capture NVLink utilization and GPU memory footprint, we suspect baseline has higher memory copy overhead
06:38 Jin: will do, i'll enable nvlink counters on the run
06:45 Samir: quick note on cost - our Optimize suggestions (batching + cache) when applied reduced per-token cost by ~18% in the last run vs baseline numbers; we'll include a cost worksheet in the deck
07:05 Maya: that's promising, pricing will be important for our procurement
07:10 Priya: on security, can you confirm KMS integration and where logs live? we need to feed to our SIEM
07:18 Samir: yes, KMS/HSM supported for private deployments, logs can be forwarded via syslog or S3 and we have audit log streams. i'll include the SOC2 and log retention details in the packet
07:30 Diego: any differences we should be aware of between hosted vs dedicated pool vs private in terms of latency?
07:37 Jin: hosted (what you're on for pilot) is tuned for multi-tenant throughput with our batching heuristics, dedicated pool gives more predictable p99 because you remove noisy neighbors and can tune batch windows bigger; private on-prem is similar to dedicated but adds network hop depending on your infra - we typically see a small delta if on-prem networking isn't optimized
08:10 Maya: baseline provider mentioned they can do a shaved kernel set for lower token latency - did you try kernel-level optimization?
08:20 Jin: good question - we have an automated kernel selector and we deployed a trimmed kernel build for this run; the baseline had a slightly different kernel set which explains their slightly better cold-start single-token numbers. But our continuous batching and KV caching provide better end-user experience under load
08:45 Diego: any anomalies in the raw logs? errors or timeouts?
08:50 Jin: we saw a handful of transient 502s during one of baseline comparative runs when their autoscaler was spinning up; Redwood had fewer transient errors under identical synthetic load
09:05 Priya: latency variance - do you have histogram images in the sheet?
09:10 Jin: yes, sheet tab 'histograms' has them, and there's a note explaining p95 bump corresponds to the 30s spike when we introduced a cold connection to the backend
09:25 Maya: on the prompt side, we have a bunch of long contexts (2-4k tokens). how does caching behave there?
09:33 Jin: for long contexts we chunk kv entries and keep prefix cache; the hit rate drops with completely unique contexts but for your application we observed ~65% hit rate for the top 20 templates, which are the common flows
09:50 Diego: can we see a breakdown by route? i.e., embeddings vs generation vs rerank?
09:56 Jin: yes - embeddings are cheaper and latency is low (p50 ~20ms), generation is what we focused on here. Rerank (batching several docs) benefits a lot from batching and pushes throughput higher
10:20 Maya: are there any vendor lock-in concerns around your caching approach? e.g., moving to private infra later, will cache priming scripts still work?
10:30 Samir: yes they will; priming scripts are part of the deployment recipes, and KV storage semantics are consistent across hosted/dedicated/private
10:40 Diego: procurement question - what's required for an SLA for dedicated pools? minimum commit?
10:46 Samir: dedicated comes with monthly commit tiers; we'll send the commitment options but the typical enterprise pilot moves into a 3-6 month reserved capacity for SLA
10:55 Priya: when you run the 2k test, please also run with TLS + mutual auth to emulate our prod setup, that tends to add CPU overhead
11:03 Jin: noted - we'll run both TLS and non-TLS and capture CPU impact
11:10 Maya: any thoughts about model quant variants for cost savings? e.g., 4-bit vs 8-bit?
11:18 Jin: we've got quantization profiles for 4-bit (nf4) that reduce memory a lot and can cut cost ~25% with minimal quality regen for many prompts; we'll include a recommended quant profile per route in the next spreadsheet
11:35 Diego: what about fallback policies? if capacity spikes, can traffic route to a cheaper baseline for specific routes?
11:42 Samir: yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants or regions; we can configure route-level policies so critical flows stay on dedicated while non-critical go to lower-cost pools
12:05 Maya: let's talk success criteria - we want p95 < 400ms for main search flow and sustained throughput to handle 2k conc with <1% errors. Does that sound ok?
12:18 Samir: that's reasonable. jin, can you commit to a run that demonstrates that?
12:22 Jin: yes we'll run the 2k scenario with dedicated pool and primed cache and share raw histograms; if we don't hit it we can try dedicated pool tuning: bigger batch windows + adjusted kv TTLs
12:40 Diego: how long do we need to keep the pilot logs for your analysis?
12:46 Samir: 30 days should be fine, but we can store them longer if you want - will coordinate with your infra
13:00 Priya: sending firewall rules - you'll need to open outbound to our collector, i'll paste exact CIDR in email after the call
13:10 Samir: thanks, we'll watch for it.
13:20 Jin: quickly going through the linked artifacts: benchmark CSV (tabular), histograms pngs, priming script, eval prompts, and cost worksheet. All links in the notes
13:35 Maya: any risks we should flag now before the next run?
13:40 Jin: risk: if cache hit rate is lower than expected for the real traffic, p95 will increase; mitigation: we can do a small staged roll with traffic capture and offline replay to measure real hit rate first
13:55 Diego: ok please add a replay test to the next run plan
14:05 Samir: noted - add replay test to plan.
14:15 Maya: final question - timeline for procurement? we aim to decide by mid-April if the numbers look good
14:22 Samir: that lines up; next run results by 3/23 gives your team a week of analysis before procurement cutoffs
14:35 Maya: excellent. anything else?
14:40 Priya: none from infra, thanks
14:43 Samir: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the packet tonight and Jin will schedule the 2k run - meeting adjourned

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings; speaker labels best-effort. Links mentioned: sheet://nexa-poc-benchmarks (benchmark CSV + histograms), gist://priming-script, doc://security-packet

End of transcript.
